{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Licence and Hosted Platform Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Contract review findings (customer-side)  
**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **13 deviations or gaps** (3 critical, 4 high, 6 medium/low), against **5 clauses that are compliant**. The document as drafted is materially one-sided: risk allocation runs almost entirely against us.

The three critical items are structural. First, indemnification runs one way only — we indemnify Licensor broadly, Licensor gives no indemnity at all, and Article XIII expressly excludes Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. Second, the liability cap is one-sided (Licensor only) at one half of amounts paid, with our own liability expressly unlimited and no carve-outs for confidentiality, data security, indemnities or IP. Third, the Agreement is silent on ownership of our trade, order and client data flowing through the hosted Platform, and customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) becomes Licensor-owned Licensed Technology with no licence back and an express bar on modification.

Compounding these, the commercial lock-in is severe: a 36-month term with no convenience right for us, a unilateral seven-year renewal option exercisable by Licensor alone, a blanket assignment prohibition with automatic termination on any change of control, and a Licensor right of first refusal over a sale of our business. Exit is unmanaged — licences cut off immediately, we return Licensor's materials in five days, and Licensor has no obligation to return or export our data. Warranties are a pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no remedy, and there is no insurance covenant despite Licensor hosting the Platform and processing our trade data.

On the positive side, governing law (New York, SDNY or New York State courts, no arbitration) is at our preferred position; the licence is non-exclusive with no sole-supplier or non-compete restraint on our business; fees are purely usage-based with no minimum volume or take-or-pay; there is no MFN; and there are no liquidated damages or termination penalties payable by us.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | One-way indemnity from us; no Licensor indemnity, and Article XIII excludes Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement. Walk-away case. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | Silent on our trade/order/client data; paid-for customizations under Article VII(b) become Licensor-owned with no licence back and a bar on modification. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Cap is Licensor-only at one half of amounts paid (below our 6-month floor); our liability unlimited; no Excluded Claims carve-outs. Walk-away case. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Blanket assignment ban on us with no affiliate/M&A carve-out; Article XX auto-terminates on change of control; Article XXII adds a Licensor ROFR over a sale of our business. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | Grant runs to Licensee alone, access limited to our employees; Affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them. Walk-away case. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | 36-month term with no convenience right for us; Licensor may terminate immediately on any breach (no materiality or cure), change of control or wind-up. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | Licence expressly non-exclusive; no sole-supplier or requirements obligation. Article XXII ROFR raised under ASSIGN instead. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | No LDs, penalties or fee acceleration; Article XXIII bars termination damages. Audit cost-shifting on a 5% discrepancy is customary reimbursement. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | Article II restrictions and "Field of Use" limit only use of Licensor's own technology — ordinary licence scope, not a restraint on our business. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 | Unlimited audit frequency fails even the once-a-year fallback. Independent auditor, 30-day lead time and cost allocation already at our preferred position. |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Binds only us, runs three years post-termination (beyond the 24-month limit) and covers all Licensor and Affiliate employees. Advertising carve-out is acceptable. |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | Unilateral seven-year extension exercisable by Licensor alone, no opt-out for us; inconsistent with the mutual-extension mechanic in Article IV(II). |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Licences cut off immediately, Licensor materials returned in five days; no transition assistance and no obligation on Licensor to return or export our data. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER | Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, title) with no conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS | New York law, exclusive jurisdiction of SDNY or New York State courts in New York City; no arbitration. At our preferred position. |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. | Volume-tiered per-trade pricing with a rebate mechanic in our favour; no MFN or price-matching obligation. |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | 50+ US$5.00 | Fees purely usage-based per US$1m traded; no minimum volume, take-or-pay or shortfall charge, and no usage caps. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite Licensor hosting the Platform and Hardware and processing our trade data. |

## Walk-away items

These sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating currency:

1. **No Licensor indemnity, plus an express exclusion of Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement** (Article XIII). We have inserted the standard Licensor indemnity — IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct — with usual procedure.
2. **One-sided liability cap at one half of amounts paid, with our liability unlimited and no carve-outs.** We have made the cap mutual at 12 months' fees with standard uncapped Excluded Claims.
3. **Blanket assignment prohibition and automatic termination on change of control** (Article XX). We have added the affiliate/successor carve-out and removed the change-of-control termination; the Article XXII ROFR should also come out.
4. **Licence excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them.** We have extended the grant and permitted-access wording to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confidentiality-bound.
5. **36-month term with no convenience right for us.** We have inserted a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund and no penalty; 60 days' notice is an acceptable fallback.
6. **Unilateral seven-year renewal exercisable by Licensor alone.** Replaced with 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement and an uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
7. **Unlimited audit frequency.** Limited to once per 12 months, business hours, confidential auditor, no system access.
8. **No transition assistance and no return of our data on exit.** We have inserted six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter; 90 days' assistance is an acceptable fallback.
9. **Pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no warranty and no remedy.** We have inserted a 90-day conformance warranty, a workmanlike-services warranty and a no-malicious-code warranty with the standard remedy, carved out of the disclaimer.
10. **Three-year, one-way non-solicit covering all Licensor and Affiliate employees**, beyond the 24-month limit. Narrowed to a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the engagement.

## Next steps

1. **Return the marked-up draft** with the redlines described above, leading on the three critical items (indemnity, liability cap, data and deliverables ownership) as gating issues.
2. **Escalate the lock-in package internally** — 36-month term, unilateral seven-year renewal, change-of-control auto-termination and the Article XXII ROFR — for a business decision on acceptable exposure before we trade positions.
3. **Confirm the data position with the business:** identify what trade, order and client data resides on the hosted Platform and in what format we need it returned, to support the TRANSITION and IP redlines.
4. **Add the insurance covenant** (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, certificates on request) to the general provisions; fallback of E&O 1M plus cyber 2M is available if pressed.
5. **Flag internal inconsistencies to Licensor** — the unilateral renewal option versus the mutual-extension mechanic in Article IV(II) — as drafting points to be resolved in our favour.
6. **Hold the compliant clauses as-is:** governing law, non-exclusivity, absence of MFN, absence of minimum commitments and absence of liquidated damages require no change and should not be reopened."}
